items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had Ronnie Cuber. He suggested we needed a drummer.

ctx.x: Yeah. I’m saying – I’m looking at you, saying, if I’d have left you behind, brother, wouldn’t have nothing to talking about here. Sure enough, we’re on the last night of the gig at the Palm Cafe. Now we got a go-go girl on the stand. We’re playing go-go. Here’s what’s incredible. The club owner hated jazz music, but he didn’t know it. He didn’t know jazz music when he heard it. So once I found that out, I said, “Hey, I thought this fool was going to fire me. He don’t even know” – I said, “Play another jazz tune.…

But on this particular – toward the end of the night, there weren’t that many people in the place. The go-go girl, it was her time. She’d get the last 20 minutes of the show. She’s up there dancing. Then I see this guy come in. He’s a Caucasian guy. He has sloppy pos – he’s got a newspaper in his pocket. But his wife is just immaculate, with diamonds and rubies on, and hair fixed beautifully. I said, [Benson sings a corny ending riff]. The go-go girl looked at me. I said, “Get down, get down.” I started playing…
